message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to up‑to‑date weather or environmental monitoring feeds, so I can’t tell you what the current air quality index (AQI) is in Los Angeles at this exact moment.  

For the most accurate and timely information, check one of the following trusted resources:

| Source | How it works |
|--------|--------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Real‑time AQI readings from EPA‑approved stations across the U.S., including Los Angeles County. |
| **EPA’s Air Quality System (AQS)** | Historical and near‑real‑time data sets if you want deeper analytics. |
| **Local news outlets** (e.g., *Los Angeles Times*, KABC, KNBC) often report on daily AQI levels during high pollution events. |
| **Mobile apps** such as “Plume Labs – Air Report” or “Weather Underground” give city‑wide AQI dashboards. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities today, those sites will let you see whether the AQI falls into categories like Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, etc., along with recommended precautions.
